title: The Gap Nobody Knows
coreMove: Turn a declared ambition into a reality-tested operating path before treating it as a real plan.
sourcePressure: Diagnostic opening: execution is the missing link between aspirations and results, belongs to leaders, and has to live in culture through what is inspected, rewarded, and tolerated. No named company case or study is frozen for this chapter.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Make execution sound like generic accountability or post-strategy effort.

hook: the execution gap that nobody sees until it is too late
a meeting room where every plan sounds good
a generic promise colliding with reality
counterintuition: Most leaders think X, but the opposite is true
The problem is not effort, it is discipline
Execution is not about working harder
tryThisNow: set a timer and write three priorities
audit one goal in your notebook
ask yourself what matters most today
examples: generic project kickoff with vague owners
student team with a deadline and no specificity
family calendar scene used as a management analogy

exampleSpecs.domain: a regional medical-device launch whose regulatory packet has cleared but installation owners are unnamed
exampleSpecs.audience: a launch lead in a midsize manufacturer
exampleSpecs.stakes: hospitals expect delivery dates that the field team cannot yet support
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Sarah stops the launch approval when the rollout board has dates but no named owner beside the hospital installation dependency
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A laminated launch board hangs beside three unopened calibration kits while Sarah reads the blank owner column.

exampleSpecs.domain: a city library renovation grant moving from council approval into construction sequencing
exampleSpecs.stakes: the grant can be clawed back if accessible entrances are not finished by winter
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: James asks who owns the accessibility ramp permit and lets the silence expose that approval was mistaken for readiness
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Who owns the ramp permit?" James asks while the contractor folder stays closed on the table.

exampleSpecs.domain: a university lab transferring a successful prototype into a shared clinical trial workflow
exampleSpecs.audience: a principal investigator with a grant milestone
exampleSpecs.stakes: a promising device can lose trial access because intake steps are unowned
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Camille traces the missed trial window back to the week everyone celebrated the prototype without assigning patient-intake ownership
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Camille nine days after the missed trial window to notice the patient-intake line in the binder had no initials.

exampleSpecs.domain: a specialty bakery adding wholesale accounts before oven capacity and delivery routes are tested
exampleSpecs.audience: a founder moving from retail into wholesale
exampleSpecs.stakes: new cafe accounts can sour if first-week deliveries fail
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Thomas asks the team to predict the first failed delivery route, then maps oven batches and van slots until the hidden gap is visible
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Which promise breaks first: the almond croissants or the 6:30 a.m. van slot?

exampleSpecs.domain: a community theater announcing a summer festival before volunteer crew leads are confirmed
exampleSpecs.stakes: ticket sales create public commitments the crew cannot yet carry
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Anya replaces the celebratory poster review with a crew-lead board that shows which stages have no accountable person
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Fresh ink from the festival posters fills the room before anyone looks at the empty crew-lead board.

exampleSpecs.domain: a Toronto cybersecurity team promising a migration window before rollback responsibility is assigned
exampleSpecs.stakes: a failed migration could lock out payroll and customer support on Monday
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Kiran turns the migration promise into a row of named owners, rollback triggers, and tested assumptions before the window is approved
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You have the migration email ready, but the rollback column on Kiran has no owner yet.

skillTargets: spot the gap between verbal alignment and operating readiness
choose the question that forces ownership into a plan
judge when culture is rewarding launch theater instead of follow-through

tryThisNowSpec: Pick one live promise and write the next owner, the untested assumption, and the first follow-through check on the same line.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
